newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bonds fall, depos, forwards firm, ecu/drs idles.
newsitem.headline: Greek bonds fall, depos, forwards firm, ecu/drs idles.

text.p: Greek depos and forex forwards were trading a tenth of a point higher from one-week to one-year tenors on funding for bonds to be auctioned on July 15, dealers said.

Bonds came under renewed pressure in early dealing and yields on the 10-year bond rose five to seven ticks, dealers said. Ecu/drachma was hovering around 309.60 and mark/drachma dipped to 157, traders said.

"Shorts are trading around 10 percent but one-week to one-year depos and forex forwards are up 10 to 25 basis points on what seems to be funding for the upcoming bond auction," a dealer at a private bank said.
Yields on three-, five-, seven- and 10-year bonds were up five to seven basis points in early dealings to 10.03, 9.78, 9.53 and 9.35 percent respectively.

"We are under pressure again and yields are rising," said a senior bond dealer at a private bank. "Some banks think they will buy the bonds cheaper at the auction and others fear they will not find better bids later, so they sell."
A segment of the market is short-sighted and is not willing to carry the bonds when the cost of carry is negative, the dealer said.
"There is money to be made in Greek coupon bonds but it is going to take a few months," the dealer said.

Greece will seek bids for a further 75 billion drachmas each of five- and seven-year bonds with coupons of 9.2 percent and 8.9 percent respectively, and 120 billion drachmas of 8.8 percent, 10-year bonds on July 15, the finance ministry announced late on Thursday.
The five- and seven-year bonds were auctioned for the first time ever on March 19 and bids were re-opened on June 17. The 10-year bonds were auctioned for the first time on June 17.
Greece will also auction 150 billion drachmas of seven-year floating rate notes on July 29.
The mark was quoted at 156.96/01 from Friday's 157.155 fix, the dollar at 279.04/14 drachmas from 276.110 and the ecu at 309.52/62 from 309.50 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma opened at 309.65 and is currently trading at 309.55," said a forex dealer at a private bank. "The drachma is up against the mark on a higher ecu/mark."
